data.gender_notes: Thecla is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Thecla is a Greek name meaning 'expatriate' or 'student'. In early Christian tradition, Thecla is a virgin and disciple of St. Paul, known for her miraculous healings and unwavering faith. The name Thecla carries the meaning “Expatriate, student” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Thecla usually hope their child will grow to embody expatriate, student and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of dedication and commitment to spiritual growth.
data.etymology: Thecla belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Expatriate, student.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Thecla total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: תקלa
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם תקלa נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'תקל' שפירושה יפה או שלמות, ומשויך לנצרות הקדומה ולמסורת האלוקית. הוא קשור לנושאים של יופי ושלמות רוחניים.

in_greek.name: Θέκλα
in_greek.meaning: Θέκλα: το θέλημα του Θεού, ήθος ή καλλονή
in_greek.long_meaning: Θέκλα προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'θέλημα' και 'Θεός', δηλώνοντας το σχέδιο ή τη βούληση του Θεού. Στη Καινή Διαθήκη και την Παλαιοχριστιανική περίοδο, το όνομα Θέκλα συμβόλιζε την πίστη και την αρετή.

in_latin.name: Thecla
in_latin.long_meaning: Thecla derivatur ex Graecis vocibus 'thek' et 'theos', significans voluntatem seu pulchritudinem Dei. In primo Christianismo, nomen Thecla fuit symbolum fidei et virtutis.

in_english.name: Thecla
in_english.meaning: Thecla: God's will, beautiful, or virtuous
in_english.long_meaning: Thecla originates from Greek roots, signifying 'God's will' or 'beauty'. It is associated with early Christian tradition and symbolizes spiritual beauty and devotion. The name Thecla conveys a sense of piety and moral excellence.

data.cultural_impact: Thecla is an intriguing figure in early Christian literature and tradition, particularly in the City of Thecla, an ancient urban center today known as Denizli in modern-day Turkey. Thecla's story has been passed down through Greek, Syriac, Coptic, and Latin texts, and her influence has been felt beyond the shores of the Mediterranean. In this light, Thecla has played a significant role in the spread of Christianity, inspiring generations of faithful followers and contributing to a global tradition of spiritual exploration and devotion.
data.spiritual_significance: Thecla's story is a powerful reminder of the transformative power of faith and determination. Despite facing numerous challenges and obstacles in her journey towards a deeper relationship with God, Thecla remained steadfast and true to her beliefs. In her pursuit of spiritual growth, she became a model for later generations, embodying the virtues of courage, self-sacrifice, and unwavering faith. Through the history of her veneration, Thecla's story continues to serve as a source of inspiration and guidance, inviting us to deepen our own spiritual practices and cultivate our faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Thecla is derived from the Greek word "theos," meaning "divine" or "goddess." In early Christian tradition, Thecla was a disciple of Saint Paul who renounced a betrothal to her fiancé and chose a celibate life devoted to Christ. Her name represents the divine dedication and commitment to spiritual growth.

biblical_reference.note: Thecla is mentioned in the New Testament as a follower of St. Paul.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Grace Thecla in London, United Kingdom credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Thecla, which means "Expatriate, student". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
